- **Facts now record the identifier the value carries at its source.** A fact said `powo` without saying which POWO record, so the trail stopped at the database name. `GET /api/v1/species/{id}/facts` now returns `source_record_id`, including on rejected claims — the ones you most want to trace back.

Hardening of the data provenance system, driven by curating real species rather than by reading the code.

## Source arbitration
- **A tie no longer overwrites.** Only a strictly stronger source may replace a value that is already filled. When two sources of equal authority disagree, the existing value stays and the newcomer is recorded as a conflicting fact, instead of the outcome depending on which pipeline ran last.
- **Values that predate provenance recording are no longer defenceless.** They carry no f

- Source arbitration at ingestion: a weaker source no longer silently overwrites a stronger one (conflicting claims are kept and visible), implausible values are rejected before they reach the database, human-accepted corrections always win

A Python `set` cannot hold the members SurrealDB allows - `set<object>` raised `unhashable type: 'dict'` and lost the whole response - and a plain `list` loses the type, so writing a record back either failed on a schemafull field or silently turned it into an array and dropped the deduplication. `SurrealSet` is a `list` subclass that re-encodes under the set tag, so both hold.
